Warp every image the same way: corners, points or polar.

four_corners maps four source points onto four target points (warpPerspective); three_points maps three (warpAffine); log_polar and linear_polar unroll the image around a centre (warpPolar), so a rotation becomes a shift. Points are x, y fractions of the image, top-left first, clockwise. Done once when the images are prepared: OpenCV on the CPU workers, in canvas order with the other steps done once; every epoch reads the result. Same result in training, validation and test.

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Method | `method` | Choice | `four_corners` | `four_corners`, `three_points`, `log_polar`, `linear_polar` | The run | Warp. |
| Source points | `source_points` | Text | `0,0, 1,0, 1,1, 0,1` |   | The run | x, y of each point in the input (fractions 0 to 1) |
| Target points | `target_points` | Text | `0,0, 1,0, 1,1, 0,1` |   | The run | Where each source point goes (fractions 0 to 1) |
| Interpolation | `interpolation` | Choice | `linear` | `nearest`, `linear`, `cubic`, `lanczos` | The run | Corners and points: how pixels between are read. |
| Centre x | `center_x` | Number | `0.5` | `0-1` | The run | Polar: centre x (fraction) |
| Centre y | `center_y` | Number | `0.5` | `0-1` | The run | Polar: centre y (fraction) |
| Radius | `max_radius` | Number | `0.5` | `>0` | The run | Polar: radius as a fraction of the shorter side. |
| Inverse | `inverse` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Polar: from polar back to the image. |
| Output width | `width` | Integer | `0` | `>=0` | The run | Corners and points: output width, 0 = the input's. |
| Output height | `height` | Integer | `0` | `>=0` | The run | Corners and points: output height, 0 = the input's. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Data pipeline (run the graph, **Run step**, previews) | No: Image Warp is a training image step done once when the images are prepared: OpenCV on the CPU workers; PipelineExecutor image transforms are not implemented |
| Training (the compiled model) | Yes, as a preprocessing step |

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.

## Usage

```text
Resize -> Image Warp (four corners) -> Normalize -> Conv2D
```

```text
Done once when the images are prepared (OpenCV, CPU), in canvas order before the first random step. Runs in training, validation and test.
```

## Tips

- Straighten a fixed camera's view.
- log_polar: a rotation becomes a shift.
